For the Terai Tea Co. Ltd.
Mr. Supratim Dhar ...

For the State Mr. Sagar Bandyopadhyay, learned counsel appearing for the Terai Tea Co. Ltd./appellant, has submitted that the appeal preferred by the State being FA 4329 of 2004 was dismissed on 6th March, 2008 by the Lazima court in view of non-compliance of filing of the paper book.
However, the appeal and the applications were disposed of by a coordinate bench on 19th July, 2016.
Since the law is well settled, the appeal cannot be dismissed for non-filing of the paper book.

The coordinate bench proceeded on that basis and disposed of the appeal on 19th July,
2016.
Since the said appeal has now been revived by reason of the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the appeal has been filed by the State of West Bengal.

In view of the order passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on 20th February, 2018 remanding the matter at the instance of the Airport Authority of India Ltd., the requiring body, the appeal is now required to be heard on the quantum of compensation under the West Bengal Land Acquisition Act,
1894.
We are of the view that in view of the aforesaid order, Airport Authority of India Ltd. is required to be heard.

Under such circumstances, we direct Mr. Bandyopadhyay to serve copy of the paper book within two weeks from date upon prior service to learned Additional Solicitor General, Eastern Region and upon Mr. Supratim Dhar, learned counsel representing the State.
Mr. Bandyopadhyay has submitted that Cross-objector wants to file supplementary paper book.
Such leave is granted upon prior service to learned ASG and upon Mr. Dhar within the aforesaid period.
